Error classes

Source: R/conditions.R
yourhonor-errors.Rd

Every error yourhonor raises about what it was given carries one family class and the umbrella class yourhonor_error, so a caller can catch a family with tryCatch() or rlang::try_fetch() without matching message text. Message wording is for people and may change; the classes are the contract.

Details

  • yourhonor_input_error: an argument or data set the caller passed is malformed, inconsistent, or missing something required (a column, a label universe, a unique identifier, a whole-number count).

  • yourhonor_judge_error: the caller's judge function broke its output contract (wrong shape or length, keys it was not issued, a label outside the declared universe).

  • yourhonor_policy_error: acceptance_policy() was given an invalid threshold, or a policy cannot be applied to the calibration it is assessed against (it names a coefficient the calibration did not compute, or is not a policy at all).

  • yourhonor_binding_error: secondary evidence cannot be bound to the calibration it is reported with: the audit_id values differ, or an artifact that requires binding was asked to carry unbound evidence.

Errors that signal a bug in yourhonor itself ("Internal error: ...") carry no family class. Errors raised by rlang's own argument helpers (for example an unknown choice for output or format) carry rlang's classes, except in acceptance_policy(), which re-signals them as yourhonor_policy_error with the original as parent.

Examples

res <- tryCatch(
  agreement(data.frame(a = "x", b = "y"), rater_cols = c("a", "b")),
  yourhonor_input_error = function(err) "bad input"
)
res
#> [1] "bad input"
